relevance_note: Case report of a Japanese girl with HA20 caused by 'a novel de novo 119 kb microdeletion containing only TNFAIP3', plus a literature table of four earlier patients with TNFAIP3 deletions.
method_note: Read the full paper and Supplementary Table S1 by hand; a Python script in my scratch directory assembled the JSON, copied every span from the paper text (thin spaces U+2009 preserved) and sliced Table 1 cells by column. I checked the sliced cells against Table 1. Table 1 shows patients as columns: data column 1 is this report's patient (labelled 'patient', since the text describes her as the single patient of the case report); columns 2-5 are previously published patients ('Table 1 column 2' = Shimizu et al., columns 3-4 = Tsuchida et al., column 5 = Franco-Jarava et al.), with the References cell copied into source_reference_in_review. Scope: the mother (II-2) and father (II-1) are included as tested relatives (CNV analysis of the patient and her parents; SNP array of the patient and father). The grandparents are mentioned only as a group whose DNA was extracted and whose c.305A>G genotype is shown in the pedigree figure; their number and results are not given in text, so they get no rows. No variant rows for TNFAIP3 c.305A>G (NM_001270507.2): the authors describe it as relatively common (MAF = 0.0117) in the Japanese population and use it only to infer the deletion; the patient's apparent homozygous (A/A) call and the mother's heterozygous (A/G) call are therefore not recorded as variants. The '5 of 69 patients' deletion tally and the other cited reports are counts only and give no individuals. Not recorded as features: HLA typing (B51, A26 negative), infection tests (T-SPOT, EBV-IgM/IgG, C7-HRP, stool culture), WBC 18,060 cells/uL (no reference range), 'afebrile' at 8 months (a time-point state, not an exclusion of recurrent fever), and screening at 1 month 'not consistent with primary immunodeficiency, autoinflammatory disease, or hemophagocytic syndrome' (diagnostic conclusions). Age at last evaluation left not reported: she is described at 8 months (= Table 1 age at diagnosis) but seton drainage continued for 1 year after placement, and no later age is given. Checklist judgements: thyroiditis (Table 1 column 4) is not stated as autoimmune, so 'autoimmune thyroiditis' is not reported; perianal ulcers alone (column 2) not counted as gastrointestinal ulcers; psychomotor delay (column 5) not counted as CNS involvement; hepatosplenomegaly not counted as lymphoproliferation. Internal inconsistencies noted: (1) the marker variant is written c.305A>G, yet the father's G/G genotype is called 'homozygous for the reference allele' and the patient is A/A; (2) the deletion is 187 kb by EXCAVATOR2 (CNV from WES) and 119 kb by SNP array, described once as 'within the TNFAIP3 gene' and once as 'involving only TNFAIP3'; (3) IL-10 '<2 pg/ml (normal, <5 pg/mL)' is within the stated normal range, but the text calls serum IL10 levels low (recorded as stated).
